The record is complete and unimpaired on both sides, so this can be decided on the papers, and it comes out the same way whichever version of the route is taken. POL-RD-22 measures the deviation from the platform's own recorded distances: the trip record shows 4.6 km recommended against 5.2 km actual, a deviation of 0.60 km, against POL-RD-22's tolerance of 1.0 km. The GPS trace's shorter 4.315 km reading does not enlarge that figure — POL-RD-22 expressly bars re-measuring distance from a sparse trace, and the trace instead confirms which route was taken and when (off the recommended route at Jalan Bilal at 11:30:14, back on at Siglap Road at 11:35:16). The LTA traffic advisory for Bedok Road across the trip window is type NONE, so under POL-RD-23 the reroute was not traffic-justified, and the driver's explanation about bus stops and slow traffic lights is not supported by the traffic data.

That places the case squarely in POL-RD-24 row (e) — not traffic-justified, deviation 1 km or less: no refund, within tolerance. On the driver's claims: I accept the 0.60 km deviation (5.2 - 4.6), its within-tolerance status, the finding that traffic did not justify the reroute, and the excess-distance-fare figure of 0.43 SGD (0.60 km x 0.72 SGD/km, no surge) carried in the fare breakdown. The driver is also right that his omission of an in-app deviation notice is immaterial here. On the rider's claims: I accept that the vehicle deviated, that the recorded deviation is 0.60 km and within tolerance, that the traffic record does not justify the reroute, and that the arithmetic yields 0.43 SGD rather than the 2.00 SGD contested. I reject the rider's request to escalate under POL-GEN-26 because the driver's notice is not established: whether the driver notified the rider only bears on POL-RD-24 rows (a) and (b), both of which require a deviation over 1 km. On a 0.60 km deviation row (e) applies whether or not notice was given, so no fact the matrix needs is missing and there is no open question for a human reviewer.

Because the rider filed and is owed nothing, POL-GEN-03 gives NO_ACTION: the present state stands, the 9.42 SGD metered fare (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.0) is not disturbed, and both money fields are null. The contested amount is 2.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI decides finally; neither profile carries a fraud flag, and POL-RD-25's 0.80 confidence requirement is met. No clause produces a referral.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

To the rider and the driver: the record decides this case, and both sides in the end read it the same way. On POL-RD-22 the deviation is the platform's own recorded distances, 9.5 km actually driven minus the recommended 8.1 km = 1.40 km (EV-TRIP-05004), and 1.40 km is over the 1.0 km tolerance. On POL-RD-21 the driver did not inform the rider before or at the point of the deviation: the trip record's messages-during-trip list and in_app_calls are empty, the chat log (EV-CHAT-05004) holds only the two pre-trip pickup messages (08:35:52 and 08:36:12) against a deviation at 08:42:55, and the driver's own statement concedes it ('Forgot to inform, sorry'). The rider's 'Ok' at 08:36:12 cannot be an acknowledgment of a deviation that had not yet happened. So this is not row (a) of POL-RD-24, and the within-tolerance no-refund rows (c) and (e) do not apply either. What is owed is fixed by POL-RD-24's excess-distance formula: deviation distance 1.40 km x the metered rate 0.72 SGD/km (EV-FARE-05004) = 1.008, rounded to the cent as 1.01 SGD, which is the ledger's own derived excess_distance_fare_sgd. I note the one open question in the record: whether the LTA HEAVY_TRAFFIC advisory (EV-ADVIS-05004-01) intersects the recommended route, so as to make the reroute traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. It does not change the money, because if it is justified the case is row (b) and if it is not the case is row (d), and both rows refund the same excess distance fare. I therefore do not need to resolve it, and neither side asked me to. The rider asked for 4.00 SGD, but POL-RD-24's measure is distance-only and without surge: the 2.80 SGD base fare, the 3.24 SGD time fare, the 0.90 SGD platform fee and the 1.00 SGD ERP charge all sit outside the formula, and the ERP was incurred on the PIE at 08:40:36, before the 08:42:55 deviation, and is carried on the optimal route too. The rider is owed 1.01 SGD, not 4.00 SGD and not nothing, so under POL-GEN-03 the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of 1.01 SGD. Every artifact relied on is COMPLETE with weight_multiplier 1.0 and no issue codes, so my confidence is not capped below 1.0; I set it at 0.90 against the 0.80 POL-RD-25 requires for a route deviation. The disputed value is 4.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so this AI ruling is final; there is no safety flag and no fraud flag, no escalation under POL-GEN-26 arises because every fact the refund row needs is carried by complete evidence, and no clause adds a referral. The 1.01 SGD is returned to the rider; the driver keeps the rest of the metered fare.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

Both of you agree on the shape of the trip; you disagree on whether the detour was justified by traffic, and the evidence decides that against the driver.

Deviation (POL-RD-22): the platform's recorded distances give 14.6 km actual less 12.7 km recommended = 1.90 km, above the 1.0 km tolerance. This is not a within-tolerance case, so rows (c) and (e) of the refund matrix are unavailable.

Traffic justification (POL-RD-23): a reroute is justified only where traffic data that intersects the recommended route shows congestion, an incident or a closure. The advisory covering the recommended route — the AYE towards the City, Clementi Road to Keppel Viaduct (EV-ADVIS-05006-01, valid 17:29–18:59, overlapping the trip) — records no incident, roadwork or closure; its type is NONE and its own derived field marks it as not justifying a reroute. The second advisory (EV-ADVIS-05006-02) is a roadwork, but it sits on Pasir Panjang Road towards Telok Blangah — a road on the route the driver actually took, not on the recommended route (Clementi Avenue 2, AYE, Keppel Road, Wallich Street). I resolve that advisory's open intersection field: it does not intersect the recommended route, so it cannot justify leaving it. The driver's real-time assertion of a jam is not traffic data under POL-RD-23. The reroute is not traffic-justified.

Notification and agreement (POL-RD-21): the driver did inform the rider in-app before deviating (MSG-05006-003 at 18:01:46, read 18:02:06) and the rider acknowledged with 'ok' (MSG-05006-004 at 18:02:11), both before the platform recorded the deviation at 18:05:06. That limb is met. But the rider's agreement is decisive only in row (a) of the refund matrix, which also requires the reroute to be traffic-justified — and it is not.

Refund matrix (POL-RD-24): row (d) applies — not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km — and it refunds the excess distance fare in full. That figure is 1.90 km × 0.72 SGD/km = 1.37 SGD, no surge, and it is exactly the 1.37 SGD already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver on 19 August 2026 (payment_status PARTIALLY_REFUNDED).

Outcome (POL-GEN-03): the driver filed contesting that refund. The rider is owed the 1.37 SGD, so the driver's claim is not supported and the present state stands: NO_ACTION, with both amounts null. Nothing is returned to the driver, and no further sum is refunded to the rider — the 1.37 SGD she holds is the amount the policy requires. No clause in this category produces a referral, so none is added.

The driver's alternative request — hold the sum for review if the reroute is found unjustified — is declined. The facts POL-RD-23 turns on are carried by the two advisories and the trip record, so there is no open question for POL-GEN-26 or POL-RD-24's no-row rule to escalate. Confidence: all eight artifacts are COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the deciding facts (the 1.90 km deviation and the absence of traffic justification) carry full weight (POL-GEN-02). The contested amount is 1.37 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD line, so the ruling is final at any confidence; neither profile carries a fraud flag; POL-RD-25's 0.80 bar is met.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

To both parties — here is what the record shows and what follows from it.

The deviation is measured, not guessed. EV-TRIP-05005 records 13.8 km driven against a recommended 12.1 km, a deviation of 1.70 km (POL-RD-22), which is above the 1.0 km tolerance, so the 'within tolerance' no-refund rows do not apply. EV-GPS-05005 and the platform's event log agree the car left the recommended route at the TPE / Upper Serangoon Road exit at 10:21:30.

Driver: the timing of your message decides your defence. You sent MSG-05005-003 at 10:24:30 (EV-CHAT-05005), about three minutes after you had already left the recommended route at 10:21:30. POL-RD-21 requires you to inform the rider before or at the point of deviation, and a message sent after the turn is not that notice, however courteous. The rider's one-line 'ok noted' at 10:25:00, opened at 10:25:10, does not convert a completed deviation into an agreed one under row (a). Your counter-statement says you informed her 'before I changed route'; the chat and event timestamps contradict that, and the record carries no call recording, so a verbal notice cannot be established (POL-RD-21, POL-GEN-26).

What does help you is traffic. EV-ADVIS-05005-01 records an LTA vehicle breakdown on the KPE towards ECP, valid 09:59:38–10:54:38, on the expressway the recommended route uses and within the trip window, so I accept the reroute was a response to real traffic, as POL-RD-23 requires. That puts the case in POL-RD-24 row (b) — traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km — which refunds the excess distance fare. Row (d) would give exactly the same figure if the traffic question were resolved the other way, so the amount does not turn on it.

Rider: you are owed the excess distance fare, not the 5.00 SGD you asked for. That fare is the deviation distance at the metered per-km rate, without surge: 1.70 km x 0.92 SGD = 1.564, rounded to 1.56 SGD (EV-FARE-05005, POL-RD-24). EV-FARE-05005 records the 23.04 SGD fare charged with 0.00 SGD refunded, so 1.56 SGD is returned to you and the balance of the fare stands.

On who decides: the contested sum is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither profile carries a fraud flag, so no human review is required; POL-RD-25's route-deviation threshold is met at a confidence of 0.90, above the 0.80 required, and its 2 km limb is switched off in any event (the deviation is 1.70 km). Every figure above comes from artifacts the pre-pass grades COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so nothing is discounted for impairment. No clause in this category produces a referral.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
